 Order

The petitioners have filed this petition under section 482 of Cr.P.C seeking to quash the charge sheet in C.C.No.82/2024 pending on the file of learned Additional JMFC Court, Hosapete, for the offences under Sections 3, 6A and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 ("E.C.Act" for short), under Sections 3, 4, 12, 18 and 19 of the Karnataka Essential Commodities (Public Distribution System)
Control Order 2016 ("PDS Control Order, 2016" for short) and under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code ("IPC" for short) insofar as petitioners-accused Nos.4 and 5 are concerned.

Control Order 2016

sentences.text:
2. It is the case of the prosecution that the complaint came to be lodged on 23.09.2023 on 9.00 a.m.,
by the Food Inspector, Hosapte alleging that on the same day, he received a credible information that some persons were being illegally transporting rice bags, which were to be distributed to the beneficiaries under various schemes in a Tata Canter Vehicle and the accused persons have illegally obtained the rice meant for public distribution and intended NC: 2024:KHC-D:9781 to sell the same in a black market after polishing the same and he has filed the complaint against the unknown persons.
3. Based on the above complaint, the SHO of respondent No.1 registered the case and after securing the panchas, the Police Sub-Inspector of respondent No.1 Police Station along with his staff went to near APMC market, HLC Canal, Ballari and when they were watching, at about 10.30 a.m., one canter lorry came from Ballari, in order to go to Harihara road and after seeing the raiding party, the driver of the canter lorry moving the same in a slow manner and when the raiding party have intercepted the same, there was rice loaded in the lorry, hence, Police Sub-Inspector, made enquiry,
but the driver has not produced any document and he has revealed the name of one Ajmir-accused No.1 resident of Kushtagi taluk and he also revealed that, on the instruction of one Sharabayya-accused No.3, the said rice bags were loaded in the lorry bearing registration No.KA.63/7632 belonging to accused No.2 and hence, the Police Sub-Inspector seized in all 14,000/- Kgs., of rice and arrested accused No.1.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:9781 4.
Based on the information given by accused No.1, the Investigating Officer, proceeded with the investigation and filed charge sheet against accused Nos.1 to 5.

Taking exception to the same,
accused Nos.4 & 5 have filed this petition.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the lis stands covered by the judgment rendered by the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of T.Thippeswamy son of Sanna Thippaiah and another Vs. State of Karnataka and another in Crl.P.No.5130/2023, disposed off on Manche Gouda S/O Boregouda vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37515487/
3 29.08.2023, wherein, the identical issues have been raised and have been answered in favour of the petitioners therein.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Boregouda vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has held at paragraph Nos.10 to 13, which are as follows:
10.
The offense which has been alleged against the petitioners is for transporting rice allegedly meant for the Public Distribution System without valid license.
For that particular purpose, it is required to prima facie establish that indeed the rice was belonging to the Public Distribution System and that the petitioners had no right over the same.

It is but required that in respect of these prima facie evidence, the invoices and payment receipts, if any, produced by the petitioners/transporters would have to be verified by the Investigating Officer before filing a charge sheet.

In the present case, perusal of the charge sheet indicates that no such effort has been made and the invoices which are produced along with the present petition, which have been placed before the Investigating Officer have not been considered.

12. That apart, whether the rice belonged to the Public Distribution System or not could only be ascertained by necessary examination by the Forensic Science Laboratory and a report being submitted thereto.
The Investigating Officer has not caused such an examination and has gone ahead with the sale of rice on the premise that the same is perishable goods which require immediate sale.

Even if the goods are perishable, it is required for the Investigating Officer to send the said rice for necessary examination to the Forensic Science Laboratory and a report is to be obtained from the said authority.
13.
In the present case, neither of the above have been done.

Hence, I am of the considered opinion that there is no legs for the prosecution to stand on and prosecute the petitioners and prima facie there is nothing made out to establish the offense being committed by the petitioners.
As such, there would be no purpose in prosecuting the petitioners on such frivolous grounds without any basis.

6. Learned High Court Government Pleader would not dispute the position of law as is observed in the case referred supra.
7.
In view of the issue in the lis standing answered by the Court quoted on all its force, the subject petition also deserves to be succeeded.

8. For the aforesaid reason, I pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:9781 : ORDER :
i.
The criminal petition is allowed.
